category_title: Successful readers who focus on text and meaning-making
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-class explicit phonics lesson on decoding rules and digraphs.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at the board and practice our phonics rules for digraphs.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I’m not too big on reading, but I love books.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We need to practice breaking these words apart first.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Phonics is really boring, but it helps you to read.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please pay attention to me while I explain how to code these words.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Turns away from the teacher and focuses on reading the posters and charts on the wall instead of attending to the instruction.)

STUDENT: I’m not too big on reading, but I love books.

task.content: Explicit phonics instruction focused on decoding rules, identifying sounds, counting sounds, defining terms (digraph), and applying diacritical marks (coding).
task.learning_goal: Students learn to decode quickly and effortlessly by applying explicit rules.

context.environment: Classroom during direct instruction and guided reading
context.materials: Posters and charts on the walls, instructional texts being used, diacritical marks for coding, picture clues, items from home (The Important Bag)
context.social_setting: Whole-class direct instruction and guided reading groups

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: During direct instruction when the teacher is presenting content
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Reads the posters and charts on the walls rather than attending to the teacher. Focuses on the texts that are being used rather than the teacher.
related_quotes: Phonics is really boring, but it helps you to read.
I’m not too big on reading, but I love books.

behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: More often focused on the texts that were being used than on the teacher
